abstract: Let N_λ(X) count coprime triples a+b=c≤X with rad(abc)<c^λ. We generalize a two-letter collision inequality and obtain N_λ(X)≪X^{54/91+ε} for 0<λ≤1, with the sharper certified exponent 5588/9417. The inequality allows arbitrary coprime exponent pairs on one letter and arbitrary nonempty sets of free coordinates on a second. Its proof uses a Bézout parametrization in the unit group and uniform bounds for differences of powerful monomials. We also determine exact program values at five radical budgets and derive a piecewise-linear envelope β(λ) on [0.70,1.10] by reusing rational Farkas multipliers. This envelope improves throughout that interval on the minimum of the trivial bound and the applicable bounds of Bernert, Browning, Lichtman and Teräväinen. In particular, the exponent 3/5 remains valid up to λ=247/245. The arithmetic constraints and rational certificates establish the upper bounds; feasible points describe their limitations. The supplement provides the certificates, independent exact verifiers, numerical comparisons and a reproducible figure. The manuscript was produced with substantial AI assistance and has not been reviewed by a human expert.
author: lihongmin
change_summary: 1. Corrected the Section 6 comparison intervals at μ=9/11 and μ=21/23, clarified the corollary comparison argument, and rechecked every comparison breakpoint in exact rational arithmetic, retaining the minimum gap 311/47085. 2. Qualified the optimality statements: the symmetric feasible points give lower obstruction bounds, and further instances of this family cannot force a bound below 213/359. 3. Added a reproducible comparison figure (300 dpi PNG and PDF) generated from the exact parametric output, replaced the interleaved table by the figure while retaining exact values in the supplement, and shortened the abstract to fewer than 250 words. These are local corrections and presentation changes; no change to theorems, proofs or certificates.
title: Collision inequalities and the radical budget for the exceptional set in the abc conjecture
